title: Injective middle term: the Cech local-lift cocycle is the connecting class
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let 0 \to A \to I \to Q \to 0 be a short exact sequence of sheaves of O_X-modules with I injective in Mod(O_X) [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and let U = {U_i} be an open covering of X. For q in H^0(X,Q), choose lifts x_i in I(U_i) of q|_{U_i}. Then (x_{i_1}|_{U_{i_0} cap U_{i_1}} - x_{i_0}|_{U_{i_0} cap U_{i_1}}) is an A-valued Cech 1-cocycle, and the canonical map c_A from Cech H^1(U,A) to H^1(X,A) sends its class to the connecting class partial(q) for this short exact sequence.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 01EQ (cohomology-lemma-cech-cohomology), proof via the double complex and the maps beta followed by alpha^{-1}, together with Lemma 01EP (cohomology-lemma-injective-trivial-cech)

proof.text: On each overlap U_{i_0} cap U_{i_1}, the image of x_{i_1}-x_{i_0} in Q is q|_{U_{i_0} cap U_{i_1}}-q|_{U_{i_0} cap U_{i_1}}=0, so exactness puts this difference in A. On a triple overlap, the alternating sum (x_{i_2}-x_{i_1})-(x_{i_2}-x_{i_0})+(x_{i_1}-x_{i_0}) is zero by cancellation, hence these differences are a Cech 1-cocycle by the differential in [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex].

Use the canonical comparison map described in [lem-sc-cech-comparison-map-naturality]: for an injective resolution A \to J^bullet, the total complex has maps alpha_A from global sections and beta_A from the Cech complex, with alpha_A a quasi-isomorphism, and c_A is H^1(alpha_A)^{-1} H^1(beta_A) followed by H^1(Gamma(X,J^bullet)) = H^1(X,A). Thus the c_A in the statement is the map used by the total-complex computation.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 01EQ proof via the double complex, together with Lemma 01EP (lemma-injective-trivial-cech)

proof.text: Since I is injective and A \to I is a monomorphism, choose an injective resolution A \to J^\bullet with J^0=I and J^q=0 for q<0 (continue by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives]). Exactness of J^\bullet gives Q=I/A \cong \mathrm{im}(d^0) \subset J^1, so s_C: Q \to J^1, with the complex K^n=J^{n+1} and differential -d, is an injective resolution of Q. Let q~ in J^1(X) be the image of q; then d(x_i)=q~|_{U_i}. Horseshoe: put I_B^n=J^n \oplus J^{n+1}, d_B(a,b)=(da-b,-db), s_B(x)=(x,dx), \alpha^n(a)=(a,0), \beta^n(a,b)=b. Direct checks: d_B^2=0, \alpha and \beta are cochain maps, \alpha^0 s_A=s_B f, \beta^0 s_B=s_C g, each 0 \to J^n \to I_B^n \to K^n \to 0 is split exact, and s_B is an injective resolution of I (a cocycle (a,b) of I_B has b=da, so (a,b)=(a,da)=d_B(0,-a) is a coboundary in degrees \geq 1, and the degree-0 cocycles are \{(x,dx)\}=s_B(I)). So (J,I_B,K,\alpha,\beta) is a horseshoe resolution of 0 \to A \to I \to Q \to 0 as in [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor] (compare [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-ses]), and \delta^0(q) is computed by the snake: lift q~ in K^0(X) to (0,q~) in I_B^0(X); d_B(0,q~)=(-q~,0)=\alpha^1(-q~). Hence partial(q)=-[q~] in H^1(\Gamma(X,J^\bullet)), transported to H^1(X,A) by the isomorphism \iota_J of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift]. Total complex: in Tot(Cech(U,J^\bullet)) with d=d_I+(-1)^p d_{II} [def-sp-double-complex-total] and d_Cech(s)_{i_0i_1}=s_{i_1}-s_{i_0} [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex], the 0-cochain (x_i) in Cech^0(U,J^0) has total differential (x_{i_1}-x_{i_0}) + (q~|_{U_i}) = \beta_A(c)+\alpha_A(q~), where c=(x_{i_1}-x_{i_0}) is the A-valued cocycle of Step 1. So H^1(\beta_A)[c]=-H^1(\alpha_A)[q~], and by Step 2 c_A[c]=-[q~]=partial(q).

split_report.summary: Split the injective-middle case of the Cech-to-cohomology comparison. The local differences x_{i_1}-x_{i_0} form an A-valued Cech cocycle; c_A is the alpha/beta comparison map; an injective resolution of A starting with I gives an explicit horseshoe, whose snake boundary is -[q~], and the total-complex computation gives c_A of the cocycle as -[q~], hence partial(q).
